page: Microsoft Azure D64pls_v6 is an ARM-based virtual machine belonging to the Dplsv6 server family. It is powered by a Microsoft ARM Neoverse-N2 processor running at 3.4 GHz, featuring 64 physical cores and 64 vCPUs with a dedicated 1.0 thread-per-core allocation. The system is equipped with 128.0 GB of memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per core. Cache specifications include 64 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 128 MB of L3 cache. This instance does not include local storage or GPUs, but it is Premium Storage capable and runs on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor.

In benchmark evaluations, the D64pls_v6 demonstrates strong multi-core scaling and memory performance. Multi-core CPU performance via stress-ng and Geekbench multi-core scores both rank in the top tier (top 10%). Large-block memory bandwidth read and write operations also achieve top-tier status, alongside Passmark memory scores and database operations. Single-core performance, including stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core metrics, falls within the average range. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and Passmark CPU physics tests also reach the top 10% tier, while static web serving throughput and Redis SET operations show strong performance in the top 25%.

Given its 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the D64pls_v6 is configured as a low-memory, compute-focused ARM instance. This hardware profile offers qualitative cost efficiency for highly parallelized workloads that require substantial CPU core density without the overhead of large memory footprints. It is well-suited for multi-threaded tasks such as software compilation, database operations, static web serving, and parallelized data decompression. However, workloads requiring high single-threaded performance or massive memory-to-CPU ratios may find this configuration less optimal.
